title: Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt
capsule: The Fifteenth Dynasty (c. 1650–1550 BCE) was the principal Hyksos dynasty of ancient Egypt, ruling the Nile Delta and Middle Egypt from the capital at Avaris (modern Tell el-Dab'a) during the Second Intermediate Period. The Hyksos — a Semitic-speaking people from Canaan who had migrated into Egypt over several generations — introduced the horse-drawn chariot, composite bow, and bronze weapons to Egypt. The six known Hyksos kings of the dynasty included Salitis, Khyan, and Apophis (Apepi), with Apophis's long reign representing the dynasty's apex; the Kamose Stelae record his boast of ruling from Avaris to Kerma. The dynasty was expelled from Avaris around 1550 BCE by Ahmose I of the Eighteenth Dynasty, ending Hyksos rule in Egypt and inaugurating the New Kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of the Fifteenth Dynasty is moderately attested from Egyptian administrative papyri and archaeological evidence at Avaris (Tell el-Dab'a), but its precise southern border with the Seventeenth Dynasty remains debated.
